Thank you

Wait. Why? Ssdp supply unique identiferers. That should be used here.

If two devices swap ip (dhcp), this change would block those config entries from being updated.

> Wait. Why? Ssdp supply unique identiferers. That should be used here.
> 
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/45802#issuecomment-771117350
Shouldnt it at least match model names and some other key values for such stupid devices?

> Shouldnt it at least match model names and some other key values for such stupid devices?

Wouldn't that require fetching the `location` as well as assuming the `model name` won't change between firmware versions (I know I have been bitten by assuming it wouldn't)?

Maybe. I just don't like the concept of making things worse for devices that behave properly.

If the UDN matches it should update existing device hostname, not abort. This should handle working devices.

Then if we still find an existing device with same hostname and name?? Anything that is in the direct announce. We can abort.

IMHO getting duplicate entries if you change firmware woud be an okey compromise if it only happens for broken devices.

We could do something like
```
        self._abort_if_unique_id_configured(updates={CONFIG_ENTRY_HOSTNAME: discovery[DISCOVERY_HOSTNAME]})
```

This would ensure that if the ip did change the existing config entry would have the new hostname if the ip changed.

Yea that should work as first step.

The problem is if the broken device hogging a hostname is no longer turned on. No other device can take that hostname. That is why I think the abort based on hostname + name/model or something additional.. would limit the breaking behaviour to stay within one device manufacturer.

This only impacts SSDP discovery and only prevents multiple discoveries of the same device (which randomize their UDN, not according to spec), ish. Ish, because this is far from ideal but most devices (mostly routers) don't change their IP. Also, lots of devices don't supply model name or other information.

If you add the integration by hand it'll use its own discovery mechanism and it'll store the DeviceType/UDN in the config entry. After that (e.g., via restart), if the integration is activated again, the same discovery mechanism is used to locate the device with the given DeviceType/UDN. This behavior is untouched.

Devices that behave properly should hardly be impacted.

> The problem is if the broken device hogging a hostname is no longer turned on. No other device can take that hostname. That is why I think the abort based on hostname + name/model or something additional.. would limit the breaking behaviour to stay within one device manufacturer.

It is a tradeoff. Do we want to support a mostly hypothetical situation, or support the people with broken devices (Google Wifi, AsusWRT)? I suppose the latter group is a whole lot larger than the first group.

> We could do something like
> 
> ```
>         self._abort_if_unique_id_configured(updates={CONFIG_ENTRY_HOSTNAME: discovery[DISCOVERY_HOSTNAME]})
> ```
> 
> This would ensure that if the ip did change the existing config entry would have the new hostname if the ip changed.

Good point, missed that. I'll add it later.

> > The problem is if the broken device hogging a hostname is no longer turned on. No other device can take that hostname. That is why I think the abort based on hostname + name/model or something additional.. would limit the breaking behaviour to stay within one device manufacturer.
> 
> It is a tradeoff. Do we want to support a mostly hypothetical situation, or support the people with broken devices (Google Wifi, AsusWRT)? I suppose the latter group is a whole lot larger than the first group.

My point was to support both..

Feel free to create a PR. Before you start, I can tell you that you can hardly depend on information from the device (serialno, model, manufacturer, etc.) Lots of devices report nothing. Please keep this in mind.

Thanks 👍

Can you check if the UDN stays the same, @Nebby ? You can do this by configuring the device or ignoring the device. Then, look in your configuration/storage file: `core.config_entries`. You'll see something like this:
```
{
                "entry_id": "2cf54af203ff11eb889329085e3a70fb",
                "version": 1,
                "domain": "upnp",
                "title": "Ambit EVW320B",
                "data": {
                    "udn": "uuid:upnp-InternetGatewayDevice-1_0-889ffacb9043",
                    "st": "urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice:1"
                },
                "options": {},
                "system_options": {
                    "disable_new_entities": false
                },
                "source": "import",
                "connection_class": "local_poll",
                "unique_id": "uuid:upnp-InternetGatewayDevice-1_0-889ffacb9043::urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice:1"
            }
```

The line with `"udn": "..." is the some you're looking for.

I'm expecting that for all entries, there is a different UDN.

Another thing @Nebby , can you check if your router keeps the same hardware address? Usually you can see this from your own computer, running `arp` on Windows or on Linux. In Linux this gives the output:
```
$ arp
Address                  HWtype  HWaddress           Flags Mask            Iface
_gateway                 ether   xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx   C                     eth0
```

The `xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx` is the thing you're looking for. The address can be different, in my case it reports `_gateway`, but it might also be your routers' IP.

I expect the output to globally look the same in Windows.
As stated I'm expecting the `udn` to change regularly. Are there any other constants which can be used to identify the device?

Preventing a component from being discovered isn't possible. I've submitted a PR for this, but it got shot down: #43647.

There are a few options:
1. Edit the file `homeassistant/components/upnp/manifest.json` and remove the following lines. You'll have to do this every time you upgrade home assistant.
```
  "ssdp": [
    {
      "st": "urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice:1"
    },
    {
      "st": "urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice:2"
    }
  ]
```
2. Disable UPnP in your router, see page 45 in the [manual](https://dlcdnets.asus.com/pub/ASUS/wireless/4G-AC55U/E10633_4G-AC55U_MANUAL_V2.pdf). You do this once. Other applications might stop working partially related to online activites (multiplayer on game consoles, file sharing applications, ...) Although, many application can work properly without and the impact might not even be noticable!
3. Ask ASUS to fix this. The [UPnP Device Architecture document](http://upnp.org/specs/arch/UPnP-arch-DeviceArchitecture-v1.0.pdf) states on page 27:
> UDN: UDN  Required. Unique Device Name. Universally-unique identifier for the device, whether root or embedded. Must be the same over time for a specific device instance (i.e., must survive reboots).
4. I can add a configuration option to the component such that it is never activated. I'd rather not do this for a single device, but if this helps... but I would like to have #43646 merged before I make any changes to the component.
